subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should OpenClaw adopt resetSessionEntryLifecycle as a permanent public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, or narrow lifecycle rotation to an owner-routed internal runtime seam before merging this Teams fix?
rationale: The behavior fix is sound, but the branch expands a shipped external plugin contract with concurrency, harness ownership, rollback, and session-state semantics; repository policy requires maintainers to choose that long-term boundary rather than allowing review automation to infer it.

options.title: Narrow to owner-routed runtime seam
options.body: Expose a generic scoped reset request that routes to the physical harness owner while keeping the low-level store mutation private or internal.

options.title: Accept the public SDK contract
options.body: Adopt resetSessionEntryLifecycle as a supported external plugin API and explicitly own its documented compatibility and concurrency semantics.

options.title: Pause the SDK expansion
options.body: Keep the bug open and replace this branch with a narrower approach only if existing session APIs can preserve the required atomic owner coordination.

recommendation.title: Narrow to owner-routed runtime seam
recommendation.body: Expose a generic scoped reset request that routes to the physical harness owner while keeping the low-level store mutation private or internal.

likelyOwner.reason: They contributed the current lifecycle scoping decision and are the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate for this cross-cutting Teams and session-runtime boundary.
